messages:
maya: Heads-up — after last runtime build (attn-fast-v2 + new quant q4 profile) we see a big drop in prefix cache hit-rate on prod: ~90% -> ~48%. Latency p95/p99 spiked and token counts up. Noticed right after the 2026-11-02 nightly deploy.

sam: Which deploy id / commit? can you paste the deploy-bot output and a quick metric snapshot?

maya: deploy-bot shows: deploy 2026-11-02T02:14Z commit 5f4d2a3 runtime: compile/attn-fast-v2 quant-profile:q4_legacy. Infra snapshot: requests ~1200 rps, prefix_cache_hit 48%, token_cost up 22%. Attaching quick log excerpt below.

maya: ```
[prod][kvcache] keygen: model=redwood-13b-q4 prompt_hash=0x7a9f3c mask_hash=0x0021ab key_bytes=140
[prod][kvcache] miss: key=7a9f3c::0x21::len140
[prod][kvcache] hit: key=7a9f3c::0x0201::len140
[prod][kvcache] miss: key=7a9f3d::0x21::len140
```

maya: The odd part is many keys look like they only differ by a small field (e.g. mask bytes ordering or leading zero). Suspect serialization/order change in KV buffer after kernel variant swap.

leo: I saw a similar regression on a canary for llama-family q4 after switching to attn-fast-v2 — kernel changed how static KV is packed (endianness/packing of mask/seq meta). That will break any naive key-bytes serialization.

nate: short-term mitigation: we can force the previous kernel with `--kernel-variant=attn-stable` for the affected model family via runtime flag routing. That restores hit-rate in canaries but increases token compute ~4-6%. Also can bump warmup traffic to repopulate caches (we should do both).

sam: sounds good. Maya, can you validate that forcing attn-stable recovers hit-rate and measure the cost delta? If so we should rollback kernel-variant for the next hour and open a follow-up to make keying robust. @leo are you able to own the key canonicalization patch?

maya: quick test on prod-edge: forcing attn-stable -> cache_hit ~87% within 10 minutes, p99 down ~150ms. GPU utilization up slightly. Reprod steps: set route flag, restart model-workers for family redwood-13b, monitor `kv_prefix_hit` metric.

infra-bot: metric-snapshot: {"prefix_cache_hit": "48%", "request_rate_rps": "1200", "p95_latency_ms": "420", "p99_latency_ms": "890", "time": "2026-11-02T02:28:00Z"}

deploy-bot: deploy 5f4d2a3 runtime/attn-fast-v2 -> rolled at 2026-11-02T02:14Z by build-pipeline (no canary gate).

leo: I'll prototype a canonical key encoder that: 1) normalizes prompt whitespace, 2) uses fixed-order metadata fields, 3) encodes integer fields as big-endian varints, and 4) adds a version byte. That should make keys invariant to kernel packing. Will bench locally.

maya: great. Can you also add a quick regression test where we compare keys produced under attn-fast-v2 vs attn-stable for the same prompt? If they differ it's a blocker.

leo: will do. Initial plan: patch in runtime/keygen -> add canonicalization layer + unit tests. If tests pass, schedule canary rollout to 1% traffic, check prefix_hit and latency.

sam: I'll prepare a rollback note and notify SRE and CS for affected customers (we may need a short incident page). Also add a short postmortem ticket — root cause likely key serialization change tied to kernel compile.

nate: operational checklist: 1) force attn-stable on redwood-13b routes (maya) 2) run warmup traffic for 15 minutes (nate) 3) deploy leo's key canonicalization to canary (leo) 4) monitor prefix_hit / tail latency for 1h (sam/infra).

maya: I'm applying the flag now and will report back in 10m. tagging @nate for warmup. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks. after we stabilize, let's add a lint rule in the compiler that flags changes that affect KV layout or serialization. we should avoid silent regressions like this.

leo: quick note — initial local bench shows canonicalized keys identical across kernels; cost of canonicalization negligible (~0.2% extra cpu per key). I'll open PR with tests and bench results in an hour.

maya: thanks everyone — updating this thread with metrics. creating incident/infra ticket and linking the deploy id.

sam: I'll coordinate customer comms if needed.

maya: (follow-up) after forcing attn-stable hit climbed to 88% and p99 dropped to ~420ms. leaving rollback for 30m while we validate. will post final incident notes.
